the topological properties, or graph metrics of cells in tissue images of glioma can be used to identify the cancer cells and the cancerous tissues with an accuracy of over 85%.

the topological properties (graph metrics) of the cellular networks of the cells of the cancerous tissue,

the topological properties and the graph metrics of cancer cells in tissue images, and demonstrates that the topological properties at the cellular level can be used as a tool for cancer classification and diagnosis.

the topological graph metrics of the cellular graphs of the cells in the brain cancer tissue images can be used as an alternative to the histopathological diagnosis of the cancer.
the topological properties (graph metrics) of the cells within a tissue image can distinguish the cells of a cancerous tissue from the cells of a healthy and non neoplasm inflamed tissue.

we have demonstrated that the cell graphs of cancer can be used to identify cancerous cells and tissue samples.

cancerous tissue samples exhibit unique graph metrics of their cells, and that the cell graph metrics are able to correctly classify tissue samples as cancerous, healthy or non neoplastic inflammatory.
the graph metrics of cells in the tissue samples can be used to distinguish cancer cells from healthy and inflamed non neoplastic cells at both the cellular and the tissue level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell graph metrics are capable of identifying cancerous cells in the brain tissue images.

we show that the topological properties (graph metrics) of the cells are a useful feature for distinguishing between cancerous, healthy, and inflamed cells and tissue, and thus may provide a new way of classifying tissue samples in the future.
